key_insight: Constitutive-Set Mechanics replaces a single constitutive law with an admissible set and uses the structure’s own strain history to certify robust response bounds.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers quantify uncertainty in simulations when experiments do not uniquely identify material behavior, improving trust in design predictions under untested loading paths.
method: Formulate mechanics variationally over an admissible set of constitutive laws instead of one law.
Use the occupation measure of strain states to turn the set response into a support-function energy.
Extract equilibrium-based certificates for worst-case response and constitutive inference, with stronger guarantees under global minimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on linear elasticity, fracture, a finite-strain composite shell, and a membrane, including a shell where only 4 of 226 constitutive directions were interrogated and a membrane where certified worst-case energy exceeded the reference by more than fourfold.
watch_item: Results depend on how well the admissible constitutive set is specified; an incomplete or overly broad set can weaken bounds or make certification conservative.
paper_title: Constitutive-Set Mechanics: variational mechanics on an admissible set of constitutive laws
